title: 基于自适应图的机器学习优化器
abstract: This paper introduces a novel machine learning optimization algorithm based on adaptive graphs, designed to improve model performance through dynamic parameter adjustment. The core idea is to represent the learning process as a graph, where nodes represent parameters and edges represent the relationships between them. An adaptive graph is constructed that dynamically adjusts the graph structure during training, allowing the optimization process to focus on the most influential parameters and pathways. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this algorithm through a series of experiments on several benchmark datasets, showing significant improvements in accuracy and generalization ability compared to traditional optimization methods. The paper also explores the benefits of using adaptive graphs for complex, high-dimensional datasets.

title: High-Dimensional Time Series Forecasting Models: A Quantum Adaptive Learning Approach
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum self-adaptive learning to high-dimensional time series forecasting models, leveraging the unique properties of quantum computing to enhance prediction accuracy and efficiency, particularly in scenarios involving large datasets and complex feature representations. We propose a novel "Quantum Adaptive Adjustment" mechanism that dynamically adjusts the learning process based on the characteristics of the time series data, leading to improved model performance. The research focuses on mitigating the limitations of traditional machine learning algorithms in handling high dimensionality and complex patterns, presenting a promising approach for improved forecasting capabilities. The paper details the implementation of the quantum self-adaptive learning process, including the introduction of the adaptive adjustment mechanism and a comprehensive evaluation of its effectiveness through simulations and a benchmark dataset. We conclude with a discussion of the potential impact of this approach on various real-world time series forecasting tasks.

title: Title: Non-Standard Quantum State Representation: Entanglement-Driven Geometry
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of a novel quantum state representation, termed the "Geometry-Aware Entanglement Metric," to provide a deeper understanding of entanglement dynamics. Traditional quantum state representations often lack explicit incorporation of the geometry inherent in the entanglement space, hindering our ability to fully characterize and predict entanglement behavior. We propose a new representation that leverages the curvature of the entanglement space as a key metric, allowing for a more comprehensive analysis of entanglement correlations. The proposed metric, coupled with a refined entanglement analysis technique, offers a potential pathway to unlocking new insights into the fundamental properties of entanglement. This work addresses a long-standing challenge in quantum information theory by introducing a fundamentally different approach to representing and manipulating quantum states.

title: Quantum Topology: A Novel Validation Method for Geometric Transformations
abstract: Quantum topology, a burgeoning field, offers a fundamentally different approach to geometric analysis compared to traditional methods. This paper explores the potential of quantum topology to rigorously validate geometric transformations and models, particularly in the context of quantum systems. We propose a novel algorithm leveraging quantum topological properties to assess the correctness of geometric transformations, providing a robust and potentially transformative validation technique. The core claim is that this algorithm can effectively quantify the fidelity of geometric transformations, offering a pathway towards a more reliable understanding of complex geometric models. This research addresses the limitations of current validation methods and highlights the unique capabilities of quantum topology for this application.

title: Adaptive Quantum Computing Quantum Simulation Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the application of a self-adaptive quantum simulation optimization algorithm to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of quantum simulations. Traditional simulation methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting the potential for optimization. This research proposes a novel algorithm that dynamically adjusts simulation parameters based on simulation results, resulting in continuous refinement and improved performance. The core mechanism focuses on a reinforcement learning-inspired approach to optimize the simulation process. This adaptive strategy offers a significant advancement in quantum simulation, addressing limitations of static optimization techniques and promising improved results across a range of quantum systems. The paper details the algorithm's design, implementation, and results, demonstrating its potential for enhancing the capabilities of quantum simulations.

title: Probability Graph Models: An Extended Approach
abstract: Probability Graph Models (PGMs) represent complex systems as graphs of nodes and edges, allowing for the modeling of relationships and dynamics. This paper explores an extended approach to PGMs, focusing on the incorporation of dynamic probability update mechanisms to simulate the behavior of complex systems in response to external events and system changes. The core claim is that this enhanced method provides a more realistic and adaptable framework for modeling dynamic systems. The paper introduces the concept of "event-driven probability update," a novel technique for generating probabilistic responses to changing conditions. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through a simulation of a simplified system exhibiting emergent behavior. The resulting model exhibits a significant improvement in its ability to capture dynamic system behavior compared to traditional PGMs.

title: High-Order Matrix Dynamics and Quantum Entanglement
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of high-order matrix dynamics, augmented with quantum entanglement, to accelerate optimization processes, particularly within matrix decomposition and linear algebra problems. The core mechanism centers on utilizing entanglement to enhance the computational capabilities of the optimization process, aiming for significantly faster results in key areas of matrix analysis. The research focuses on demonstrating the efficacy of this approach through theoretical analysis and preliminary numerical simulations, highlighting its potential impact on the field of matrix optimization.

title: Based on Quantum Entanglement: Distributed Algorithm Acceleration
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum entanglement for accelerating distributed algorithms. The core claim is that leveraging entangled states for direct communication can overcome the limitations of classical algorithms in distributed computing scenarios. The proposed mechanism involves the development of prototype quantum algorithms that utilize entanglement for data parallelism and synchronization. This work explores a fundamentally new approach—exploiting quantum mechanical properties for intrinsic computation acceleration rather than solely optimizing existing architectures. The research focuses on building a distributed computing network based on entangled states, addressing challenges related to entanglement distribution, error correction, and algorithm design. We present a theoretical framework and outline key considerations for realizing this paradigm shift in distributed computation.

title: Self-Healing Neural Networks via Dynamic Pruning and Retraining
abstract: Neural networks have demonstrated remarkable success in various domains, but their performance can degrade over time due to concept drift – the phenomenon where the statistical properties of the input data change. This paper proposes a novel approach to mitigate this issue by designing a self-healing neural network architecture. The core idea is to dynamically prune unnecessary connections within the network and subsequently retrain it using ongoing feedback. This dynamic pruning and retraining process allows the network to adapt to evolving data distributions and maintain its accuracy. We define the self-healing process with the following equations: Let *N* be the number of neurons in the network. Let *L* be the number of layers in the network. Let *Wij* be the weight connecting neuron *i* in layer *l* to neuron *j* in layer *l+1*. Let *Sij* be the magnitude of the weight *Wij*. Let *α* be the pruning threshold (0 < *α* < 1). Let *R* be the learning rate. Let *D* be the new dataset. The pruning step involves removing connections with weights below *α* *Sij*: Pruned Weights: { *Wij* | *Sij* ≥ *α* *Sij* } The retraining step involves updating the remaining weights using the new dataset *D* and the learning rate *R*: Updated Weights: *Wij* = *Wij* - *R* *∂Loss/∂Wij* (where *Loss* is the loss function calculated on dataset *D*) This dynamic approach aims to improve the robustness and adaptability of neural networks, particularly in scenarios where concept drift is prevalent.

title: Quantum Entanglement Algorithmic Self-Organizing Adaptive Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a peculiar phenomenon in quantum mechanics, holds immense potential for advanced computation and optimization. This paper explores the concept of a self-organizing adaptive algorithm leveraging quantum entanglement to dynamically adjust parameters within a system, enabling complex optimizations and calculations beyond the limitations of traditional approaches. We propose a novel computational model centered around a dynamically evolving "quantum entanglement network," where the entanglement state itself serves as a core control mechanism for self-adaptation. This algorithm aims to address challenges in optimization and computation by exploiting the inherent properties of entanglement. The core claim is that this algorithm can achieve significant performance improvements through continuous, self-adjusting parameter manipulation. This work presents a foundational framework for exploring the application of quantum entanglement in algorithm design, highlighting potential avenues for future research and development.

title: ## Benin Tree Hyrax-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Benin Tree Hyrax Algorithm" (BTHA), inspired by the foraging behavior of Benin Tree Hyraxes. These hyraxes exhibit a unique strategy of searching for food resources within a tree canopy, utilizing a combination of exploration and exploitation. The algorithm leverages this observed behavior to create a new optimization strategy. BTHA incorporates key elements of the hyrax's foraging process, including a hierarchical search structure mimicking the tree's branching pattern, a dynamic adaptation of step size based on resource density, and a probabilistic movement strategy influenced by local food availability. The algorithm's core mechanics involve a population of candidate solutions represented as nodes within a simulated tree structure. Each node is associated with a fitness value, reflecting the quality of the solution it represents. The algorithm iteratively adjusts the position of these nodes, guided by the hyrax's observed foraging patterns. The primary objective is to find the optimal solution to a complex optimization problem. Performance evaluations are presented on a set of benchmark functions, demonstrating the algorithm's effectiveness and competitive ability compared to established metaheuristic techniques such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results suggest that BTHA offers a promising approach for tackling challenging optimization problems, particularly those with complex landscapes and sparse solutions.

title: Plan-Then-Compile: Turning a General-Purpose Coder Model into a FHIR Data Analyst
abstract: Companion artifact to the paper Plan-Then-Compile: Turning a General-Purpose Coder Model into a FHIR Data Analyst. A frozen Qwen2.5-Coder-14B-Instruct is not a usable analyst over a FHIR-derived clinical database: given a complete schema description it answers roughly a third of familiar-concept questions correctly and three-fifths on rarer ones, never reproduces a correct query verbatim, refuses unanswerable questions unreliably, and writes queries 4.5–12× slower than gold. Fine-tuning with DoRA on 10,696 examples (9,680 execution-verified queries plus 1,016 unanswerable questions) raises execution correctness on a disjoint held-out patient population to 100.0%, and on clinical concepts appearing nowhere in training to 89.1% (85.0–92.1% across three seeds). Two design decisions carry the result: Terminology is resolved through the database. Gold SQL never embeds a literal SNOMED/ICD-10/RxNorm code; every query resolves its clinical concept at runtime via a lookup against a valuesets table. This converts an unverifiable memorization problem into a checkable query-composition one, and makes generalization to unseen clinical vocabulary measurable. An ablation shows that merely making this table visible in the schema drives the untrained model's terminology-hardcoding to zero. Plan-then-compile targets. Each training target pairs a structured JSON query plan with the compiled SQL in one continuous completion, so clinical-entity isolation and query-archetype identification become inspectable artifacts rather than latent steps. A subsequent DAPO/GRPO reinforcement-learning stage adds nothing measurable: all three seeds early-stop at step 40 of a 200-step budget having peaked at the first evaluation checkpoint, with mean reward pinned at or above the correct-answer floor on 37–38 of 40 steps — supervised fine-tuning already saturates the reward's correctness gate. Scope and honesty notes. All data is synthetic (Synthea); no real patient data is used. The held-out familiar arm is 96.5% verbatim training rows and its abstention set is reused from training, so those results demonstrate retention rather than resistance to memorization; the unseen arm shares no question, query, or clinical concept with training and is where transfer is established. Its 89.1% is an upper bound — because unseen concepts are rare and their gold answers are small integers, 53.9% of within-archetype concept pairs return identical results — with text-match metrics giving 81.4% as a lower bound. Contents: corpus-generation and verification scripts, the frozen benchmark schema, assembled datasets, both training notebooks and the ablation notebook configured as run, and all per-seed training logs, evaluation summaries, failure logs and ablation results. Licensing: code (scripts/, notebooks, schema/) is Apache-2.0; the paper, documentation and data are CC-BY-4.0. title: 基于量子纠缠的并行计算模型
abstract: This paper investigates a novel parallel computing model predicated on the principles of quantum entanglement. Traditional parallel computing approaches often rely on classical communication and computation, limiting the potential for significant performance gains. We propose a model that leverages quantum entanglement to facilitate data transfer and computation, offering a fundamentally different approach to parallel processing. The core mechanism centers around establishing entangled states between processors, enabling instantaneous and correlated data exchange and acceleration of computational processes. This paper explores the theoretical foundations, implementation challenges, and potential applications of this approach, highlighting its promise for advancing the capabilities of parallel computing. The research explores the benefits of this model through a detailed analysis of entanglement properties and its implications for data manipulation and calculation.

title: Cognitive Graph-Based Program Adaptive Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to program optimization termed Cognitive Graph-Based Program Adaptive Optimization (CGBPAO). The core concept revolves around constructing a cognitive graph representing the runtime state of a program. This graph facilitates autonomous learning and adaptation of execution paths, allowing the program to dynamically respond to evolving environments and data. The system leverages deep learning techniques to generate this cognitive graph in real-time, where nodes represent program states and edges signify relationships between them. Subsequently, optimization algorithms operate on this graph to intelligently select pathways, effectively transforming the program into a dynamic "intelligent agent" capable of genuine self-adaptation. This approach moves beyond traditional static code optimization, offering a fundamentally new paradigm for program behavior and efficiency. The primary contribution lies in the integration of graph representation with deep learning for real-time adaptive control, enabling programs to proactively adjust their execution based on observed data and changing conditions. ---

title: 基于自适应的概率模型
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to probabilistic modeling based on an adaptive probability model. The core challenge in many real-world applications is the difficulty of accurately modeling complex data and the need for automated parameter tuning. Traditional methods often rely on manual parameter adjustments, which can be time-consuming and suboptimal. This paper introduces a new algorithm that dynamically adjusts model parameters based on data and prediction results, using an adaptive algorithm to optimize the parameter set. The proposed method significantly improves prediction accuracy compared to existing models, particularly in scenarios involving high dimensionality or complex relationships within the data. This work offers a robust and automated solution for probabilistic modeling, addressing a key limitation of current approaches.

This work addresses limitations in traditional matrix decomposition methods by introducing a fundamentally different approach to parameter adjustment. title: Adaptive Kernel Topology for Machine Learning
abstract: This paper presents a novel method for enhancing machine learning model generalization performance through adaptive kernel topology. Traditional kernel methods rely on fixed kernel functions, limiting their ability to effectively capture complex data relationships. We introduce an algorithm that dynamically adjusts the topology of kernel functions during training based on observed data distribution, resulting in improved performance across a range of datasets. The core mechanism involves a reinforcement learning-inspired approach, iteratively refining the kernel's structure to minimize generalization error. We evaluate the proposed method on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in accuracy and robustness compared to existing techniques.

title: Title: Adaptive Chaos Dynamics in Data Structures
abstract: This paper explores the application of Adaptive Chaos Dynamics (ACD) to the design of self-organizing data structures. We propose a novel system that dynamically adjusts the complexity of data structures—specifically, trees and graphs—in response to real-time data fluctuations, optimizing space allocation and information retrieval. abstract: Quantum-enhanced geometric simulation represents a paradigm shift in modeling complex network interactions, offering the potential to surpass the limitations of classical approaches. This work details the design of a quantum algorithm for topology representation and the implications for simulating network dynamics. The paper concludes by discussing the challenges and future directions of this emerging field.

title: Temporal Inference Based on Multi-Modal Neural Networks
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to temporal inference by constructing a multi-modal neural network model capable of simulating human time perception and reasoning. The core of this model lies in the utilization of multi-modal neurons activated by sensory inputs (visual, auditory, and motor) and a time-varying network that establishes temporal dependencies. We introduce a time-varying network that processes a sequence of probability activations from these multi-modal neurons, employing a recurrent neural network to learn and predict future events within an event sequence. Unlike existing models that primarily operate on static sequential data, our architecture incorporates contextual information and explicitly models the dynamic nature of temporal relationships. This approach offers a more robust and realistic representation of how humans perceive and infer temporal sequences, particularly when multiple modalities are involved. The key innovation is the integration of multi-modal neural networks with a time-varying network, enabling the model to learn complex temporal dependencies and generate predictions based on contextual information. The model's performance demonstrates its ability to capture nuanced temporal patterns, suggesting potential applications in areas such as event sequence prediction, human-robot interaction, and cognitive modeling. ---

title: ## Argentine Tuco-tuco: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of Argentine Tuco-tuco
abstract: This paper presents Argentine Tuco-tuco (ATT), a new metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Argentine Tuco-tuco, a burrowing rodent native to South America. The algorithm leverages the tuco-tuco's strategy of exploring a territory, exploiting resources, and adapting to environmental changes to create a robust optimization process. ATT combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA) with novel mechanisms for adaptive exploration and exploitation. Specifically, the algorithm incorporates a "territory division" mechanism, mimicking the tuco-tuco's territoriality, and an "environmental adaptation" mechanism, reflecting the animal's response to resource scarcity. The performance of ATT is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitiveness against established metaheuristic algorithms like PSO, Differential Evolution (DE), and Genetic Algorithm (GA). The results show that ATT is particularly effective in challenging landscapes with complex, multi-modal solutions. This research contributes a novel approach to metaheuristic design, drawing inspiration from the natural world and offering a potentially valuable tool for solving complex optimization problems.

title: ## The Arfak Ringtail-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (ARIMA)
abstract: This paper presents the Arfak Ringtail-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (ARIMA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the unique foraging strategies of the Arfak Ringtail (Lemur crinifrons) found in Papua New Guinea. The Arfak Ringtail is known for its efficient and adaptive search behavior when locating food sources in complex and dynamic environments. ARIMA leverages this inherent intelligence by mimicking the ringtail's exploration-exploitation balance, memory retention, and adaptive movement patterns. The algorithm utilizes a modified particle swarm optimization (PSO) framework, incorporating a 'memory ring' to retain past best positions and a dynamic adjustment of velocity based on a simulated ringtail's responsiveness to environmental changes. We demonstrate the effectiveness of ARIMA through simulations on benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to outperform traditional PSO and other established metaheuristics in terms of convergence speed and solution quality. The algorithm's design prioritizes adaptability and efficiency, reflecting the remarkable survival strategies of the Arfak Ringtail.

title: Dynamic Topology for Probability Inference
abstract: This paper presents a novel probabilistic inference algorithm based on dynamic topology. Traditional probabilistic inference methods often rely on fixed models, limiting their ability to effectively handle complex data. Our algorithm leverages dynamic topology to derive probability inference results, significantly enhancing the accuracy of the process. The core mechanism centers around the inherent structural properties of dynamic topologies, which offer a powerful framework for generating and evaluating inference models. We introduce a novel technique for constructing and manipulating topological structures to optimize inference, leading to improved results compared to existing approaches. The algorithm's design incorporates a robust method for analyzing and refining the resulting topological structures, ultimately yielding more accurate and reliable probability inferences.

title: Antonio Brack's Oldfield Mouse: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by a Unique Animal Behavior
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Oldfield Mouse Algorithm" (OMA), inspired by the foraging behavior of *Mus musculus oldfieldensis*, a subspecies of the common field mouse known for its complex and seemingly random movement patterns within a defined territory. The algorithm leverages the mouse's exploratory strategy, incorporating elements of both random search and local search, to effectively navigate solution spaces. OMA's core mechanism revolves around simulating the mouse's movement, utilizing a probabilistic distribution based on its observed foraging behavior. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, with each individual representing a potential solution. The distance traveled by each individual is determined by a random number and a bias towards areas with previously lower visitation rates. Furthermore, OMA incorporates a 'return to base' mechanism, mirroring the mouse's tendency to periodically revisit its central territory. This paper details the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and a preliminary analysis of its performance on several benchmark optimization problems. The results demonstrate OMA's potential as a competitive metaheuristic for a variety of challenges. The key mathematical components include probabilistic movement models, distance calculations, and population management strategies. The algorithm aims to achieve a balance between exploration and exploitation, ultimately converging towards optimal or near-optimal solutions.

Addressing a critical bottleneck in machine learning, this approach offers a potential solution for faster and more accurate model training.

title: Dynamic Topological Quantum Error Correction Code
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense potential across various fields, and the development of robust quantum error correction (QEC) is crucial for realizing this potential. Traditional QEC relies on encoding logical qubits into highly entangled states, making them vulnerable to decoherence. This paper proposes a novel dynamic topological quantum error correction code based on the unique properties of quantum error correction. We introduce a "dynamic topological" mechanism that dynamically adjusts the quantum state's topology during evolution, enhancing the code's resilience against noise and enabling more efficient quantum information processing. The core claim posits that this approach surpasses classical QEC by offering enhanced robustness and adaptability. This work explores the theoretical foundations and initial experimental validation of this innovative concept, demonstrating its potential for significantly improving QEC performance.

title: Quantum-Driven Geometric Chaos Simulation with Adaptive Parameterization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum-driven geometric chaos simulation technique designed to enhance the accuracy and robustness of complex system representations. Traditional geometric chaos simulations often rely on fixed parameter settings, which can limit the system's ability to explore intricate dynamics. We propose a quantum algorithm that dynamically adjusts geometric chaos parameters during simulation, allowing for a more adaptive and comprehensive exploration of the system's behavior. This approach leverages quantum evolution to mimic the inherent complexity of geometric chaos, resulting in improved modeling capabilities. The system is modeled as a discrete geometric space, and the quantum process evolves the system's configuration, adapting parameters to the system's dynamics. This paper explores the potential of this method for simulating various complex systems, including those exhibiting fractal-like structures and sensitive to initial conditions. The core mechanism involves a quantum process to evolve the system's geometric configuration, adapting parameters to the system's dynamics.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel system of framework for predicting system states and enabling collaborative control utilizing graph neural networks (GNNs). We propose a GNN architecture that learns node representations based on the graph topology, enabling the model to effectively capture dependencies and predict future states. title: 基于多模态神经符号推理的动态知识图谱构建与更新
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for constructing and dynamically updating knowledge graphs (KGs) based on multi-modal neural symbolic reasoning. The core idea is to leverage the strengths of deep learning for understanding complex semantic information from diverse data modalities (images, text, audio, etc.) and traditional knowledge representation methods through symbolic reasoning. The proposed system employs a multi-modal encoder to map data from various modalities into a unified embedding space. Subsequently, a neural symbolic reasoning engine, utilizing Transformer-based models, performs inference to derive new entities, relations, and attributes from these embeddings. These inferences are integrated into the KG, and continuous updates and corrections are implemented via feedback loops incorporating user interactions and external knowledge sources. Crucially, the system proactively identifies and addresses ambiguities and uncertainties within multi-modal data, translating them into probabilistic representations of relationships within the KG. This approach overcomes the limitations of static, manually-annotated KGs and enables a dynamic, autonomous KG construction and evolution process, capable of handling the inherent complexities of multi-modal data.

abstract: This paper introduces the Bluefin Optimization Algorithm (BOA), a novel metaheuristic optimization technique inspired by the foraging behavior of bluefin tuna. BOA aims to achieve efficient global convergence while maintaining adaptability to varying problem landscapes. The core mathematical representation of the algorithm is presented, outlining the parameters and equations governing its operation. This paper details the theoretical underpinnings of BOA and establishes a framework for future research and application.

abstract: Adaptive constraint optimization is a critical challenge in various fields, particularly in areas like engineering design, logistics, and finance, where finding optimal solutions within complex, high-dimensional spaces is essential. The core mechanism focuses on leveraging quantum annealing's ability to efficiently search sparse solution spaces, coupled with the neural network's capacity to learn and adapt to the problem's characteristics. The core mechanism focuses on leveraging quantum annealing's ability to efficiently search sparse solution spaces, coupled with the neural network's capacity to learn and adapt to the problem's characteristics. The paper details the algorithm's design, its performance evaluation, and potential applications.

title: Ant Colony Optimization for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, Ant Colony Optimization for Complex Optimization Problems (ACOCP), inspired by the foraging behavior of ants. The algorithm leverages concepts from Artificial Intelligence, specifically mimicking ant trail formation and pheromone deposition to navigate and solve complex optimization problems. ACOCP employs a probabilistic approach, where ants explore the search space probabilistically, guided by pheromone trails that reflect the quality of solutions found by previous iterations. The algorithm incorporates mechanisms for pheromone evaporation and reinforcement, promoting convergence towards optimal or near-optimal solutions. This paper details the algorithm's design, including the representation of the problem space, the probabilistic movement rules, the pheromone update rules, and a discussion of parameter tuning. The core formula for pheromone update is: ΔΦij = Σk=1N ηk * Tij, where Φij is the pheromone on edge (i, j), ηk is the heuristic value of ant k, Tij is the transmission rate of pheromone from ant k. The probability of choosing a neighboring node is calculated as: Pij = (Cij / Σl Cil) * (Φij / Σl Φil), where Cij is the cost of moving from node i to node j, and Φij is the pheromone level on the edge (i, j). The algorithm is then demonstrated through theoretical analysis and illustrative examples, highlighting its potential and limitations.

title: Admiralties Rat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Admiralties Rat
abstract: This paper presents Admiralties Rat, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the behavior of the Admiralties Rat, a rare and intriguing rodent known for its complex navigational strategies. The algorithm leverages the rat's ability to explore and exploit its environment efficiently to solve optimization problems. Admiralties Rat combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Ant Colony Optimization (ACO), incorporating a dynamic adaptation of the Lévy flight mechanism to enhance exploration. The core innovation lies in a novel 'Rat's Path' representation, where solutions are encoded as sequences of directional movements, mimicking the rat's route-finding process. This representation is coupled with a 'Territory Awareness' mechanism, allowing the algorithm to prioritize regions of the search space with higher potential for optimal solutions. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, Rastrigin function, and the Sphere function. Results demonstrate that Admiralties Rat consistently outperforms traditional metaheuristic algorithms in terms of convergence speed and solution quality. The algorithm's adaptability and exploration capabilities make it a promising candidate for various complex optimization challenges.

title: Adaptive Foraging Strategy Based on Capuchin Monkey Social Dynamics: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, termed the "Capuchin Adaptive Foraging Strategy" (CAFS), inspired by the foraging behavior and social dynamics of capuchin monkeys. The algorithm leverages concepts of social hierarchy, resource competition, and cooperative foraging observed in these primates to dynamically adjust its search parameters and exploration-exploitation balance. CAFS employs a population-based approach with a novel agent representation, where agents are assigned 'social ranks' reflecting their influence within a local foraging group. These ranks are updated based on individual foraging success and the overall group's performance. The algorithm utilizes a "resource awareness" mechanism, mimicking the monkeys' ability to assess the availability and quality of food sources. CAFS's core innovation lies in its adaptive adjustment of the learning rate and neighborhood size, influenced by both the agent's rank and the perceived scarcity of resources. The algorithm's performance is evaluated theoretically, demonstrating its potential for robust optimization in complex, dynamic environments. The aim is to provide a biologically-inspired approach to metaheuristic optimization, potentially offering advantages in scenarios where environmental changes and social interactions significantly impact the optimization process.

title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization for Dynamical Systems
abstract: Quantum-Inspired Optimization for Dynamical Systems explores the application of quantum mechanics principles to accelerate the optimization of complex systems exhibiting dynamic behavior. This paper introduces a novel algorithm, termed 'Quantum-Driven Momentum,' inspired by the phenomenon of quantum fluctuations, designed to efficiently navigate intricate solutions to dynamic systems. The core mechanism centers around a process that utilizes quantum fluctuations to guide the exploration of the solution space, resulting in faster convergence and improved accuracy compared to traditional optimization methods. The paper provides a detailed explanation of the algorithm's design, its mathematical formulation, and preliminary experimental validation demonstrating its effectiveness across a range of dynamic system examples.

title: Self-Adaptive Quantum Topology Verification
abstract: Quantum topology, a fascinating area of theoretical physics, offers potential for novel computational paradigms. This paper explores the application of self-adaptive quantum topology verification as a means to validate quantum computation models and optimize their parameters. We introduce a novel framework predicated on the manipulation of quantum topology to rigorously assess model fidelity, ultimately leading to improved quantum system performance. This approach departs from traditional validation methods, leveraging the inherent robustness of topological structures to provide a more reliable and efficient verification process. The core mechanism involves a dynamic adjustment of parameters based on topological analysis, promoting accuracy and minimizing error. This research highlights the potential of self-adaptive verification to significantly advance the field of quantum computation.

title: ALGORITHMS FOR REDUCING THE TIME REQUIRED TO PERFORM OPERATIONS OF THE DOMINGO-FERRER CRYPTOSYSTEM
abstract: Проведён анализ литературы по тематике полностью гомоморфного шифрования. Представлено краткое описание полностью гомоморфной криптографической системы Доминго-Феррера, основанной на задаче факторизации чисел, приведены временные характеристики этапов атаки с известным открытым текстом на данную криптосистему. Проанализированы временные характеристики операций криптосистемы, описаны методы и средства их практической реализации. Предложены новые алгоритмы реализации операций криптосистемы Доминго-Феррера, позволяющие снизить время их выполнения. Обоснование оценок временных затрат операций криптосистемы формируется на основе теоретических расчётов, а также результатов экспериментальных исследований. Целью исследования является снижение времени выполнения операций криптосистемы Доминго-Феррера посредством разработки алгоритмов их модификации, учитывающих особенности практической реализации. Основным результатом настоящей работы является снижение времени выполнения следующих операций криптосистемы Доминго-Феррера: шифрования – на 10-15%, расшифрования – в 2 раза, гомоморфного умножения – в 64 раза для цепочки из 200 умножений при использовании степени полиномов представления шифртекста d=100 и незначительном увеличении временных затрат на генерацию ключа. Проведённое исследование представляет собой значимый вклад в развитие полностью гомоморфной криптосистемы Доминго-Феррера, основанной на задаче факторизации целых чисел. Настоящая работа обладает практической значимостью, поскольку позволяет значительно повысить производительность гомоморфных вычислений данной криптосистемы. Полученные результаты могут стать основой для разработки эффективных (с точки зрения вычислительных затрат и обеспечиваемого уровня безопасности) программно-аппаратных комплексов облачных вычислений, использующих полностью гомоморфную криптосистему Доминго-Феррера для обеспечения конфиденциальности обрабатываемой информации.

title: AI ‐Augmented Memory and Consumer Sustainability: Understanding Dual Consumption Pathways in Digital Retail
abstract: ABSTRACT In digital retail, algorithmic personalisation shapes consumer outcomes, yet the cognitive mechanisms involved in this process remain theoretically underspecified. This paper introduces AI‐augmented memory (AI‐AM), a mechanism that algorithms use to record, retrieve and resurface prior behavioural traces during consumer decision‐making. The study draws on 30 semi‐structured interviews with Singapore‐based e‐commerce consumers and a complementary practitioner‐reflexive account by the researcher, based on over 10 years of multi‐platform retail experience. It examines how AI‐AM both enables and undermines SDG12 (responsible consumption and production). The thematic analysis identifies a dual pathway: a sustainable pathway, where AI‐AM reduces trial‐and‐error purchasing and supports deliberative restraint and an unsustainable pathway, where the same mechanism amplifies impulse purchase loops and erodes autonomous restraint. Four contextual conditions were associated with pathway activation: a pragmatic need‐based norm, platform‐mediated social proof, age‐associated variation in pathway responses and reliance on AI recommendations. The study extends the Engel–Kollat–Blackwell (EKB) model by theorising AI‐AM as a recursive dual‐pathway sustainability gate and develops a sustainability‐aligned design typology for platform designers and policymakers.

title: Not All Agreement Counts as Corroboration: Provenance-Conserving Multi-View Fusion for Typed Action Admission in Human-Robot Collaboration
abstract: Better probability scores do not establish that evidence has been counted correctly. Repeated inference over one observation can improve predictions without adding an evidential origin. Source-local numerical attributes alone cannot in general distinguish repeated derivations from separately countable acquisitions. PACT (Provenance-Aware evidence Conservation and Typed action admission) separates evidence magnitude from countability through a supplied provenance partition. Under singleton fidelity and insertion non-amplification, the coordinatewise meet is the unique pointwise greatest admissible within-component rule. Component budgets add under stated commensurability and separate-component additivity assumptions. Matched reassignments hold numerical outputs fixed while varying the counting relation. In four of 12 replicated-source tests on HandWritten, false refinement lowers macro-averaged negative log-likelihood and Brier score while increasing normalized common-support area under the risk-coverage curve (ncsAURC). In the controlled handover benchmark, removing the constructed adversarial-consensus condition leaves a 0.056 reduction in ncsAURC for provenance-partition aggregation relative to singleton aggregation under the same score functional. The corroboration contrast disappears, and method ranking remains selection-score dependent. In offline, reference-based human-robot collaboration with four prompts per camera and all other admission inputs fixed, duplicating each prompt output within its camera from multiplicity one to eight leaves all 720 PACT typed responses per checkpoint unchanged. Probability quality and evidence countability require separate evaluation.

title: Dicke superposition probes for noise-resilient Heisenberg and super-Heisenberg metrology
abstract: Phase sensing with entangled multi-qubit states in the presence of noise is a central theme of modern quantum metrology. The present work investigates Dicke state superposition probes for quantum phase sensing under parameter encoding generated by one- and two-body interaction Hamiltonians. Under linear collective-spin encoding, near-optimal Dicke superposition states are shown to exhibit significantly enhanced robustness against phase damping noise compared with Greenberger--Horne--Zeilinger (GHZ), W-superposition, and balanced Dicke states, while maintaining favorable metrological performance under realistic decoherence channels. For two-body interactions, optimal probe states maximizing the quantum Fisher information are identified. Their noise resilience and metrological scaling behaviour under phase damping, amplitude damping, and global depolarizing channels are analyzed. The associated near-optimal Dicke superposition states are found to exhibit improved resilience to phase damping, for the system sizes considered. These results establish tailored near-optimal Dicke state superposition probes as versatile and noise-resilient resources for Heisenberg and super-Heisenberg quantum phase sensing governed by one- and two-body interactions.

title: Photovoltaic Power Output Prediction Using PCA–KNN: A Comparative Study with SVR and MLP on Historical Operational Data
abstract: The transition toward renewable energy integration in power systems presents challenges in managing photovoltaic (PV) power output owing to variations in operating conditions. This study evaluated the performance of K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Support Vector Regression (SVR), and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), with and without Principal Component Analysis (PCA), for PV power output prediction. The dataset comprised 420 observations recorded at five-minute intervals over seven days of measurements from a PV system. The data were chronologically divided into 80% training and 20% testing sets, while normalization and PCA were exclusively fitted to the training data to prevent information leakage. The model performance was evaluated using the Mean Squared Error (MSE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), and coefficient of determination (R²). The results show that KNN and PCA-KNN achieved the best and identical performance, with an MSE of 265.3385, RMSE of 16.2892, and R² of 0.8421. PCA did not improve KNN accuracy but maintained its predictive performance after the dimensional transformation. PCA-MLP showed a slight improvement over MLP, whereas SVR and PCA-SVR yielded lower performances. These findings indicate that the effect of PCA depends on both the dataset characteristics and the learning algorithm. Further studies with longer observation periods, more diverse datasets, and external validation are recommended to assess the generalizability of the models.

title: Data for "Structured Representations and Outcome-Conditioned Output Matching in a Large Language Model"
abstract: This dataset provides the frozen research data underlying the study “Structured Representations and Outcome-Conditioned Output Matching in a Large Language Model.” It includes the fixed stimulus set, model-generated interpretations, primary and repeat judgments, analysis-unit data, stimulus-level outcome-assimilation results, frozen secondary endpoint results, and source data underlying the reported figures and tables. The deposited materials correspond to the frozen analysis reported in the manuscript and are provided to support transparency and reproducibility.

title: 弦-复共轭的量子纠缠扩展计算
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum entanglement expansion computation framework centered on the unique properties of the弦-复共轭 (弦-复) system. We propose a new quantum measurement algorithm leveraging the inherent correlations between entangled particles, aiming to surpass the limitations of classical computation. The core mechanism involves transforming the quantum entanglement process into a specialized quantum measurement algorithm that significantly expands the potential range and capabilities of quantum information processing. This work demonstrates the potential of this approach to unlock new computational paradigms and offers a distinct pathway for future quantum computing advancements. We present a preliminary implementation of the proposed algorithm and discuss its theoretical implications.

title: 基于量子纠缠的自适应数据压缩算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel data compression algorithm leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. Traditional data compression methods often rely on statistical redundancy and lossless compression, which can be limited in certain scenarios. This research explores the potential of quantum entanglement to enhance compression efficiency and robustness against noise. We propose a quantum-enhanced data compression scheme that utilizes entangled states to represent data, enabling more efficient data transfer and storage, while simultaneously improving error correction. The algorithm's core mechanism centers around exploiting entanglement to establish a higher-dimensional representation of data, reducing the overall data volume. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and preliminary experiments, showcasing significant improvements in compression ratio and resilience to noise compared to existing methods. The research highlights the potential of quantum entanglement to revolutionize data compression, offering a promising path towards more efficient data storage and transmission.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Machine Learning Model Robustness Assessment
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic adaptive machine learning model robustness assessment method. Traditional robustness evaluation methods are often static, requiring manual parameter adjustments. This approach leverages a dynamically adjusted learning process, allowing the model to adapt to data and mitigate noise and anomalies. The core mechanism involves refining model parameters based on observed data fluctuations to enhance model resilience. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through rigorous simulations and analyses, showcasing significant improvements in robustness compared to existing approaches.

title: Based on Adaptive Quantum Potential Calculation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive quantum potential calculation method, leveraging the unique properties of quantum potential calculations to optimize quantum computation performance and achieve more efficient results. Traditional quantum potential calculation methods rely on static, pre-determined potentials, while our approach emphasizes dynamic optimization to significantly enhance computational accuracy. We explore a method for iteratively refining the quantum potential landscape, enabling a more precise and efficient exploration of the solution space. The core mechanism revolves around a feedback loop that continuously adjusts the potential based on the outcome of the computation, leading to improved results. The proposed method offers a promising avenue for accelerating quantum algorithm development and improving the performance of existing quantum computations.

title: Symbolic Regression with Quantum Annealing
abstract: Symbolic regression is a powerful technique for discovering mathematical equations from data. However, the exponential growth in the solution space with increasing data complexity often presents a significant challenge. This paper investigates the potential of quantum annealing to accelerate symbolic regression. We propose a framework where a quantum annealing algorithm is directly employed to search for symbolic expressions that accurately represent the underlying relationship between input and output variables. The core idea is to leverage the quantum tunneling effect to efficiently navigate the complex, multi-modal cost function associated with symbolic regression, thereby escaping local minima and identifying optimal symbolic solutions more quickly. We demonstrate that quantum annealing can offer a viable approach to tackling this problem, particularly for datasets with moderate complexity. The approach's effectiveness stems from its ability to explore a vast solution space in parallel, a capability inherent to quantum computation. The results suggest that quantum annealing provides a novel and potentially significant enhancement to traditional symbolic regression methods.

title: Adaptive Probability Field Theory: A Novel Computational Approach
abstract: Adaptive Probability Field Theory (APFT) presents a paradigm shift in modeling complex systems by dynamically adjusting probability field parameters through neural networks. This novel approach enhances prediction and control accuracy compared to traditional methods reliant on static parameter adjustments. The core mechanism involves introducing a "dynamic probability field" that learns parameters based on environmental changes, ensuring adaptability to evolving conditions. This research investigates the feasibility and performance of APFT, demonstrating its potential for advanced modeling and control applications.

title: Quantum Computing-Based Geometric Topology Analysis
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum computing to geometric topology, specifically focusing on the analysis of quantum topological phases. We explore how quantum entanglement, a fundamental property of quantum mechanics, can be leveraged to uncover the underlying geometric structure of these phases and ultimately reveal the laws governing them. The core mechanism involves simulating quantum states using quantum algorithms, which allows for the exploration of complex geometric relationships previously inaccessible through classical methods. We present preliminary results demonstrating the potential of this approach to identify key topological features and provide insights into the formation of quantum topological states. The investigation will highlight the benefits of quantum computing in tackling challenges in geometric topology and offers a new theoretical framework for understanding these phenomena.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Programming with Probabilistic Logic Programming
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to neuro-symbolic programming that leverages the strengths of both neural networks and probabilistic logic programming. The core idea is to utilize neural networks to learn and generate logical rules, which are then executed within a probabilistic logic programming engine for reasoning and inference. This framework offers a more robust and interpretable solution for neuro-symbolic integration compared to traditional methods, by anchoring symbolic reasoning within a probabilistic framework. We present a detailed description of the architecture, including the neural rule generator and the probabilistic logic programming engine, and outline the key mechanisms for rule learning and execution. The approach addresses the challenges of brittle rule learning and lack of interpretability often associated with purely symbolic systems, while mitigating the instability and limited reasoning capabilities of conventional neural networks. Ultimately, this work demonstrates the potential for creating intelligent systems that seamlessly combine the pattern recognition capabilities of neural networks with the logical deduction abilities of probabilistic logic programming.

title: 基于自适应的量子纠缠纠错算法
abstract: Quantum entanglement is a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, offering the potential for instantaneous communication and computation. However, maintaining entanglement is incredibly challenging due to environmental noise and decoherence. This paper presents a novel approach to quantum entanglement error correction, utilizing an adaptive quantum state adjustment algorithm. We introduce a dynamic adjustment mechanism that monitors and modifies the quantum state to mitigate the effects of errors. The core claim is that this algorithm significantly enhances the efficiency and robustness of quantum error correction, offering a promising path toward practical quantum technologies.

title: Explainable Graph Neural Networks for Causal Inference
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to graph neural networks (GNNs) that integrates causal inference capabilities, addressing the long-standing "black box" problem inherent in traditional GNNs. The core idea is to develop explainable GNN models capable of discerning causal relationships between nodes within a graph, moving beyond mere correlation. We introduce causal graph embeddings, combining graph structure with explicit causal knowledge, and leverage attention mechanisms to learn and propagate causal weights. This framework allows for a more robust and interpretable understanding of complex systems, facilitating better decision-making and predictive modeling. The primary contribution lies in providing a structured method for incorporating causal reasoning into GNNs, significantly enhancing their utility in domains requiring nuanced understanding of interdependencies. Our approach offers a pathway toward building truly intelligent and trustworthy GNN systems.

title: Title: Adaptive Geometry of Quantum Computing Topology Analysis
abstract: Quantum computing offers unique computational capabilities, particularly in the realm of topological quantum information. This paper explores the application of adaptive geometry to analyze topological quantum information, investigating how quantum computation can enhance the efficiency of geometric topology. We develop a framework that leverages the inherent properties of quantum systems to model and understand topological quantum data structures. The core claim is that utilizing quantum computation allows for a significant improvement in the analysis and manipulation of geometric topology, ultimately leading to enhanced computational efficiency. The research will focus on establishing a methodology for quantifying and optimizing the impact of quantum algorithms on topological data analysis.

title: Title: Quantum-Enhanced Topological Data Analysis for Time Series Prediction
abstract: Quantum-enhanced topological data analysis (TDA) offers a novel approach to time series prediction, leveraging the unique properties of quantum mechanics. This paper proposes a new quantum algorithm designed to enhance the accuracy of predictive modeling by simultaneously exploring multiple temporal patterns. We explore the potential of quantum superposition and entanglement to identify subtle correlations that are often missed by classical methods. The core mechanism involves utilizing quantum algorithms to represent and process time series data in a fundamentally different manner, potentially leading to improved predictive capabilities. We detail the algorithm's design, its mathematical underpinnings, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating enhanced accuracy in a simulated time series dataset. The core claim centers on the potential for quantum algorithms to surpass classical methods in identifying complex, non-linear patterns inherent in time series data.

title: Bio-Inspired Neural Architecture Optimization via Simulation
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neural architecture optimization (NAO) inspired by biological neural networks. Traditional NAO methods primarily rely on mathematical optimization techniques, often neglecting the intricacies of biological neuron dynamics and adaptation. We propose a simulation-based framework that mimics the learning and adaptive behavior of biological neurons within complex environments. This framework utilizes a detailed, biologically plausible neuron model incorporating synaptic plasticity, neuronal communication, and noise adaptation, coupled with reinforcement learning to iteratively optimize the neural architecture. The core claim is that by simulating the learning and adaptation processes observed in biological neurons, we can design more robust and adaptive neural architectures. The key mechanism involves building a biologically accurate neuron model, simulating key biological processes, and applying reinforcement learning for optimization. The results demonstrate the potential of this approach to generate architectures exhibiting superior performance compared to those obtained through purely mathematical optimization.

title: Multi-Modal Quantum Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel multi-modal quantum algorithm designed to enhance computational capabilities through the synergistic integration of diverse quantum information sources. The core principle of this algorithm centers on dynamically adapting the quantum state through a carefully orchestrated interplay of various quantum states, quantum key distribution protocols, and quantum state transitions. This approach mitigates the limitations of single-information-type quantum algorithms and promises substantial advancements in computational complexity and problem-solving. The study details the algorithm's architecture, key operational mechanisms, and preliminary results demonstrating significant improvements in a range of tasks, including optimization problems and cryptography. The focus is on establishing a robust and adaptable framework for tackling complex computational challenges.

abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of anomaly detection in graph data, particularly where temporal dependencies are crucial. Traditional anomaly detection methods often fail to effectively capture the dynamic nature of graphs, resulting in missed anomalies. We propose a novel approach that leverages learned temporal graph embeddings to represent the evolution of graph structure over time. These embeddings are then used as input to graph-based anomaly detection techniques, such as graph autoencoders, allowing for the identification of anomalous patterns that would otherwise be difficult to detect. The core contribution lies in the combination of graph embedding learning with temporal anomaly detection, providing a more robust and accurate method for identifying deviations from normal behavior within dynamic graph systems. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and illustrate its potential with a conceptual framework.

title: Bismarck Giant Rat: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Bismarck Giant Rat
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, Bismarck Giant Rat (BGR), inspired by the unique foraging behavior of the Bismarck Giant Rat, a large, robust rodent known for its efficient food search strategies in challenging environments. BGR leverages the rat's adaptive movement patterns, particularly its ability to explore diverse areas while maintaining a focus on promising regions, to develop a robust and effective optimization process. The algorithm incorporates key features of the rat's behavior, including a weighted exploration-exploitation strategy, a dynamic adjustment of search radius based on local food density, and a mechanism for escaping local optima. We detail the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and theoretical analysis. The performance of BGR is evaluated through a series of benchmark problems, demonstrating its competitive capabilities against established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC). The results show BGR's efficiency and adaptability in solving complex optimization problems.

title: Bicolored Shrew Optimization Algorithm (BSOA): A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Uropsilus rutilus*
abstract: This paper presents the Bicolored Shrew Optimization Algorithm (BSOA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of *Uropsilus rutilus*, a small shrew species known for its unique and efficient foraging strategy. The algorithm mimics the shrew's ability to rapidly search for food sources by utilizing a combination of exploration and exploitation phases, guided by a novel adaptive inertia weight mechanism and a dynamic probability distribution. The BSOA incorporates elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) to achieve robust performance in a variety of optimization problems. Mathematical formulations are presented to describe the core mechanics of the algorithm, including the position update equation, the velocity update equation, and the probability calculation for food source selection. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of BSOA in solving benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The algorithm's key innovations lie in its adaptive inertia weight control and the dynamic probability distribution, which contribute to its ability to escape local optima and converge to global solutions efficiently. Future research will focus on further refining the algorithm's parameters and exploring its applicability to complex real-world problems.

title: Title: Universal Quantum State Transfer Protocol for Information Transfer
abstract: Quantum information transfer presents significant challenges due to the fragility of quantum states and the potential for decoherence. Traditional quantum communication methods, reliant on complex quantum repeaters, are limited in their reach and require substantial resources. This paper introduces a novel quantum state transfer protocol, dubbed the "Universal Quantum State Transfer Protocol," designed to overcome these limitations by leveraging entanglement swapping to enable efficient and robust state transfer across any distance, minimizing decoherence and error. The protocol's core principle centers around rapid and lossless state transfers, drastically reducing the need for complex quantum repeaters. This work explores the implementation of a unique entanglement swapping mechanism to achieve this goal, demonstrating its potential to revolutionize quantum communication. The resulting protocol offers a pathway towards more practical and scalable quantum communication systems.

title: Quantum Entanglement Adaptive Encoding
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to information encoding leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. The core idea centers around adaptive encoding, where the encoding scheme dynamically adjusts based on the characteristics of the input data and the quantum channel. This is achieved through a framework integrating entangled state generation, quantum decoy-state protocol for key distribution, and an entanglement resource optimization algorithm. The algorithm dynamically adjusts the entanglement generation and utilization based on real-time feedback, mitigating the impact of noise and interference. We demonstrate, theoretically, how this adaptive approach can significantly improve information transmission efficiency and security compared to traditional, static encoding methods within Quantum Key Distribution (QKD). The key innovation lies in harnessing the dynamic nature of entanglement, providing enhanced robustness against channel impairments. The theoretical framework outlines a robust mechanism for achieving optimal performance in QKD scenarios. ---

title: Probabilistic Programming for Simulating Complex Systems with Uncertainty
abstract: This paper explores the application of probabilistic programming languages (PPLs) for simulating complex systems characterized by inherent uncertainty. Traditional simulation methods often require significant manual effort in defining stochastic elements, handling uncertainty, and performing Bayesian inference. PPLs offer a more declarative approach, allowing users to specify the underlying probabilistic model directly, facilitating automated inference and sensitivity analysis. We argue that PPLs provide a more intuitive and efficient workflow for modeling and simulating complex systems, leading to improved understanding and decision-making in the face of uncertainty. The core mechanism involves defining a simulation model within a PPL, incorporating stochastic elements and leveraging the language's built-in support for Bayesian inference. This approach simplifies the entire simulation process, reducing the need for manual intervention and enabling more robust and reliable results. We demonstrate this principle through a conceptual framework and highlight the advantages of using PPLs for complex system simulation.

title: Ansell's Wood Mouse: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Apodemus sylvaticus*
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Ansell's Wood Mouse" (AWM), inspired by the foraging strategies observed in *Apodemus sylvaticus*, commonly known as the wood mouse. Wood mice exhibit remarkable adaptability and efficiency in locating and exploiting food resources within their environment. AWM leverages these observed behaviors – specifically, the combination of exploratory and exploitative movements, coupled with a dynamic adjustment of search radius – to construct a robust and effective optimization algorithm. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach with a novel mutation operator designed to mimic the erratic, yet purposeful, movements of the wood mouse during its foraging expeditions. We demonstrate the algorithm's performance across a range of benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to effectively navigate complex search spaces and achieve competitive results compared to established metaheuristic methods such as Genetic Algorithms and Particle Swarm Optimization. The core of AWM is the "Radius Adjustment Mechanism" (RAM), which dynamically scales the search radius based on the current population's convergence rate. The algorithm's parameters are designed to be relatively insensitive to specific problem instances, offering a degree of robustness. We provide a detailed description of the algorithm's design, its underlying principles, and a comparative analysis of its performance against other metaheuristic techniques. The results suggest that AWM holds significant promise as a versatile optimization tool, particularly in scenarios requiring adaptability and efficient exploration.

title: Dynamic Programming for Quantum Circuit Compilation with Uncertainty
abstract: Quantum circuit compilation is a critical step in the process of translating high-level quantum algorithms into executable instructions on quantum hardware. Traditional compilation techniques often rely on deterministic models of gate operations and measurement outcomes, which can lead to suboptimal results and inaccurate performance estimates. This paper introduces a novel dynamic programming approach to quantum circuit compilation that explicitly addresses the inherent uncertainty associated with qubit measurements and gate operations. The algorithm utilizes probabilistic models to represent the likelihood of measurement outcomes and gate errors, optimizing the circuit design for the *expected* performance, considering the statistical nature of quantum computation. The core contribution lies in shifting the focus from worst-case scenarios to expected outcomes, leading to more realistic and potentially more efficient quantum circuit designs. The methodology provides a framework for incorporating uncertainty directly into the compilation process, a crucial step towards achieving robust and reliable quantum computation.

title: ## Coral Crab Optimization Algorithm (CCOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Coral Crab Optimization Algorithm (CCOA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of coral crabs (Stenoplax). Coral crabs, known for their remarkable ability to navigate complex environments and efficiently locate food sources, exhibit a unique strategy involving alternating between exploration and exploitation. CCOA leverages this behavior by simulating coral crab movement within a search space, employing a "crab" representation, a "reef" structure to represent the search space, and a "current" flow mechanism to guide the crabs towards promising regions. The algorithm incorporates adaptive parameters controlling exploration and exploitation, mimicking the crabs' response to environmental changes and food availability. The core of CCOA lies in its dynamic adjustment of crab positions, reef structure, and current flow, aiming to achieve efficient convergence while maintaining a balance between exploring new areas and refining solutions around promising regions. This paper outlines the algorithm's theoretical framework, operational rules, and provides a conceptual overview, laying the groundwork for future experimental validation.

title: Andean Porcupine Algorithm: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Andean Porcupine Behavior
abstract: This paper presents the Andean Porcupine Algorithm (APA), a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Andean porcupines. The algorithm mimics the porcupines' strategy of strategically selecting and rejecting food sources, leveraging a combination of local search and global exploration. APA utilizes a novel 'spike' mechanism to represent the solution space and a 'foraging' probability to guide the search process. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions. The core of APA lies in its adaptive spike density and rejection probability, dynamically adjusted based on the convergence rate and the quality of the current solution. The proposed algorithm exhibits robust performance and offers a potentially valuable alternative to existing metaheuristic methods, particularly in problems with complex landscapes and multimodal solutions. We explore the algorithm's parameters and their impact on performance, providing insights into its design and applicability. The key mathematical formulations are presented within this document, offering a clear and concise explanation of the APA's operational principles.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Distributed Computing Optimization
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed computing optimization leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement. The core claim is that entanglement can facilitate instantaneous information transfer and coordinated optimization across distributed computing nodes, drastically improving the efficiency of complex computations. The proposed mechanism involves a distributed computing architecture where each node incorporates a quantum processor, utilizing entangled states for communication to enable parallel execution of global optimization algorithms and synchronized results. This approach aims to overcome the limitations imposed by classical communication bottlenecks, capitalizing on the unique properties of quantum mechanics to achieve significant computational gains. We explore the theoretical framework, outlining the key mathematical models and algorithms involved in this entanglement-driven distributed computing system. The system is designed to address challenges inherent in traditional distributed algorithms, offering a potential pathway toward truly scalable and efficient computation. The presented model focuses on the core principles and provides a foundation for future research and development within this emerging field.

abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum-inspired concepts to enhance the performance of random walk algorithms for optimization problems. Classical random walk algorithms are susceptible to getting trapped in local optima, limiting their efficacy in tackling complex and high-dimensional search spaces. To address this limitation, we propose a novel approach that incorporates principles of quantum superposition and tunneling into the random walk process. title: Evolutionary Algorithm for Compiler Optimization – Graph-Based Representation
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to compiler optimization utilizing an evolutionary algorithm. Traditional compiler optimization techniques heavily rely on heuristics, often failing to exploit the full potential of a program's structure for global optimization. Our method addresses this limitation by directly optimizing the control flow graph (CFG) of a program using an evolutionary algorithm. This allows the algorithm to explore a vast search space of possible code transformations, potentially discovering transformations that would be missed by traditional heuristic methods. The core of our approach involves representing the program as a graph and employing an evolutionary algorithm to iteratively refine this graph, aiming to minimize a specified cost function, often representing execution time or code size. We detail the graph-based representation, the evolutionary algorithm design, and the evaluation strategy. The results, though presented without experimental validation due to the nature of this theoretical exploration, demonstrate the potential of this approach for achieving more efficient and novel code transformations.

title: Quantum Topology: Adaptive Geometry via Entanglement-Based Computation
abstract: Quantum topology, a fascinating field at the intersection of quantum mechanics and geometry, has emerged as a promising approach for developing novel quantum computing paradigms. This paper explores a novel computational framework predicated on the dynamic alteration of geometric topology induced by quantum entanglement. We introduce a model leveraging quantum entanglement to dynamically adjust the geometry of quantum systems, thereby enhancing computational efficiency and enabling new algorithmic possibilities. The core mechanism centers around the creation and manipulation of entangled states that govern the evolution of topological structures, ultimately impacting the performance of quantum algorithms. This work presents a foundational framework for exploring the potential of entanglement-driven geometry in quantum computation.

abstract: Quantum Geometry Verification of Quantum Algorithms presents a fundamentally new method for validating quantum algorithms by leveraging the inherent properties of quantum geometry. title: Designing a Grammar Education Domain Knowledge Graph Based on Qualia Structure Structure - A focus on part-of-speech and graph RAG -
abstract: 본 연구는 AI가 문법 교육 상황에서 정확하고 체계적인 개념 설명을 제공할 수 있도록, 퀄리아 구 기반의 문법 교육 도메인 지식 그래프를 설계하고 그 작동 가능성을 탐색적으로 확인하는 데 목적이 있다. 이에 고등학교 ‘품사’ 단원을 대상으로 5종의 노드 라벨과 21종의 관계 라벨로 이루어진 속성 그래프를 설계하고 이 구조에 따라 568개의 노드와 1,793개의 관계로 구성된 문법 지식 그래프를 구축하였다.설계된 지식 그래프의 작동 양상을 확인하기 위해 일반 모델, 교과서 원문 참조 모델, 그래프 RAG 적용 모델의 생성 결과를 세 가지 문법 질문에 대해 질적으로 대조하였다. 분석 결과, 그래프 RAG 적용 모델은 ‘서술격 조사’의 분류적 위상, 구성 요소, 기능 등을 함께 제시하였고, ‘ㅂ 불규칙 활용’을 적용 조건, 변화 과정, 결과를 중심으로 서술하였다. 또한 ‘명사’와 ‘어미’를 일정한 기준에 따라 대칭적으로 대조하는 양상을 보였다. 다만 본 연구는 제한된 문항에 대한 탐색적 사례 분석이므로, 퀄리아 기반 구조의 일반적 효과는 후속 연구를 통해 양적으로 검증될 필요가 있다.본 연구는 퀄리아 구조가 국어 문법 교육 지식을 기계 가독형 그래프 구조로 표상하기 위한 설계 원리로 활용될 수 있음을 보이고, 향후 지능형 문법 튜터 구축을 위한 도메인 지식 베이스 설계의 한 가능성을 제시했다는 점에서 의의가 있다.
